target: lemma (PO_0009037), place: between the keel and marginal nerves (intercostal region); position: lowest lemma
fix: 'between them' after 'ciliate on keel and marginal nerves' is a place slot: the area between those nerves. Bind it as a place on the part instead of dropping it. Also keep 'lowest' as a position.
reason: The lemma is ciliate on the keel and marginal nerves. Only the area between the nerves is glabrous to sparsely pubescent, so 'lemma glabrous to sparsely pubescent' without the place is false for the keel and margins. 'Lowest lemma' also differs from the second lemma.
The upper-lip teeth of the calyx are ± acute, and the lower-lip teeth are too. PO has no calyx lobe or tooth class, so calyx with the approximate qualifier is a fair reading.
The leaf blade margins have shallow rounded lobes or crenate teeth. Lobed or scalloped (crenate is a PATO synonym of scalloped) are true alternatives for the blade's outline.

target: achene fruit (PO_0030107) of hermaphrodite flowers; not compressed
fix: 'ceux des fleurs femelles …, ceux des fleurs hermaphrodites …' splits the achenes by the flower they come from. The whole/position slot (achenes of hermaphrodite vs female flowers) must be kept.
reason: The same sentence says the achenes of female flowers ARE compressed. Without the hermaphrodite-flower slot, 'achene not compressed' contradicts the flora. Condensed (synonym 'compressed') is the right quality and the negation is right.

fix: When a leaf statement opens with 'basal leaves' or 'upper cauline leaves', carry that position through the whole clause.
reason: 2–8 cm is the length of the basal leaves. The same text describes other leaves, and leaf length usually changes along the stem, so 'leaf 2–8 cm' without 'basal' is not what the flora says.

The herbs are sometimes ± caespitose. Whole plant with caespitose and the approximate qualifier matches the text. 'Sometimes' is a frequency the record does not keep, but it does not make the annotation false.
The pinna (leaflet) margins are incised or pinnatifid. These are alternative incision values of the same part. 'Lacerate' is only grounded as incised, which is acceptable.
Sepals inside (adaxially) glabrous maps to the sepal adaxial epidermis.
The corolla color ranges from white to pale blue, and continuum is the right reading.

The leaves with well-developed blades are numerous, so present with the count 'many' is right.

target: leaf lamina (PO_0020039), place: abaxial surface ('au-dessous'); dull
fix: In French floras 'au-dessus'/'au-dessous' are the adaxial and abaxial surfaces, so bind them as places. Also 'limbe' is the lamina, not the whole leaf.
reason: The blade is shiny above and dull below. Saying the leaf is dull without 'below' contradicts 'brillant … au-dessus'.
The bracts are ovate, obovate or elliptic, and these are alternative shapes of the same part.
Pericarp not adnate to the seed: the bearer, the target and the negation are all right.
Petals 6.
The pod (fruit) is fusiform-clavate, an intermediate shape between fusiform and clavate.
The aerial flowering stems are 0.1–3 dm, which converts correctly to 1–30 cm.
The leaf sheath auricles of this grass are absent, and the negation is right.
The plants become brownish with age, so old context, brown and approximate are right.

fix: 'cuneate/rounded/cordate at the base' should go to the lamina base (PO_0008019), either as the bearer or as a place slot.
reason: The base of the blade is cuneate. The blade as a whole is not wedge-shaped: its apex is acute or blunt.
The leaflets are adaxially glabrous, so the adaxial epidermis substitution is right.
Stamens 5.
The monocarp's epicarp is not spiny. Fruit is an acceptable bearer for the epicarp surface, and the negation is right.
The style is equal to the corolla length. The rare 'exceeding' is an exception that does not make the main ratio of 1 false.

target: leaf sheath auricle (PO_0020106), whole: culm sheath
fix: In bamboo descriptions the culm-sheath paragraph (sheath, auricles, oral setae, ligule, 'blade erect, triangular-conical') comes before 'Leaves …'. Keep 'culm sheath' as the whole for every part in that paragraph.
reason: The context is the culm sheath (its blade is erect and triangular-conical, and the leaves start afterwards). Leaf-sheath auricles in Fargesia may be present, so the unqualified annotation can be false.
The older twigs are dull gray: stem with old context and gray is right. 'Dull' as reflectivity is not part of this annotation.
'Inflorescence compound-umbellate' means a compound umbel is present.
The male flowers are in pseudo-panicles, so the inflorescence is panicle-like. The male-flower context is minor, since the inflorescence is the male one.

fix: In orchids 'dorsal sepal' and 'lateral sepals' are separate positions, so keep 'dorsal'.
reason: Only the dorsal sepal is described as obtuse, and the lateral sepals are described separately. 'Sepal obtuse' without the position overgeneralises.

target: towards: corolla tube (fused corolla PO_0025581), place: base
fix: In 'adnate to base of corolla tube', 'base of' is a place on the target. The target is the head noun 'corolla tube', not 'base'. Resolve 'base of X' to X plus a place.
reason: The stamens are adnate to the corolla tube (at its base). The relation target FLOPO_0985024 'plant organ base' loses which organ the stamens are joined to.
